newsitem.title: UK: Russia rating rumours stir becalmed London Bradys.
newsitem.headline: Russia rating rumours stir becalmed London Bradys.

text.p: With many players away at the IMF, an absence of local news and a series of US indicators due this week, there was little to stir emerging market debt bar rumours about Russia's credit rating, dealers said.

"The speculation is that (European credit rating agency) IBCA will release its rating for Russia this week -- local sources suggest the rating will be as good as BB plus," said one eastern European debt trader here.
"Everyone's going to want to see what the big boys are going to do," added another, suggesting a good IBCA rating might influence the big two -- Moody's and Standard & Poor's.
Russian debt prices firmed during the morning, with dollar Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR climbing 1-1/8 to 70-3/4. One broker put prices as high as 71-00.
Russian Min Fins also strengthened, with the Min Fin 4 RU3E03=RR climbing 5/8 to 52-3/4.

Volatile trade in Bulgarian debt continued, with traders still gloomy about its fundamental outlook. FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR edged up 1/4 to 32-3/4 amid the on-going suspense over whether speeded up reforms were enough to persuade the IMF to release its delayed $115 million loan tranche.
Latin America was becalmed despite the launch earlier to day of Argentina's $750 million Eurobond.
Traders said the pricing, at the upper end of its indicated range of 430 to 450 basis points over treasuries, was more generous than usual for Argentina.
"The Eurobond placed a bit of a cap on (the Argentine Brady) market because the initial spread talk was over 400," said one emerging debt analyst. "People saw no big upside for FRBs."
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were quoted flat to up 1/8 at 84-00 after the launch.

Brazilian debt was unimpressed, posting little movement during the morning. Brazilian C bonds were quoted at an unchanged 70-1/2. Mexican debt was a touch softer, with Pars MX625L19=RR off 1/8 at 69-00.
A raft of US data dampened the market's energies. US National Association of Purchasing Management data due later today -- one of the big figures for Treasuries -- was drawing market attention.
One player said the market might get rattled if it comes in much about the 50 level. Analysts on average are forecasting a figure of 52.5.
Elsewhere attention will focus on the IMF/World Bank meetings in Washington. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
